Issue 1

⚔️ US-Israel Draw Up New Strike Plans on Iran as Fears of Wider War Mount

Key summary
  • Iran's IRGC declared a new 'offensive and asymmetric' defense doctrine vowing to invade any country that attacks it, warning of an 'all-out war' posture.
  • The US State Department ordered the evacuation of some diplomats and their families from Saudi Arabia citing escalating Houthi hostilities, with similar evacuation moves reported in the UAE, Jordan, Qatar, and Bahrain. Saudi Arabia's King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was hit in an attack believed to be carried out by the Houthis, killing 1 and injuring 8 (further updates expected from aviation authorities).

Issue 2

🕊️ Qatar-France Summit: Calls for Gaza Ceasefire Implementation and Reopening of the Strait of Hormuz

Key summary
  • French President Macron visited Doha, Qatar, and held a summit with Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, with the two countries issuing a joint statement calling for implementation of the Gaza ceasefire and the need to restore freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
  • Qatar and France jointly demanded Israel's withdrawal from the Gaza Strip and a halt to settlement policies in the West Bank, while also agreeing to deepen their strategic partnership and strengthen defense cooperation.
  • The Qatar Business Association (QBA) called for expanding Qatar-France investment partnerships, as both sides reviewed their overall strategic relationship, addressing diplomatic and economic cooperation simultaneously.

Issue 3

🛢️ Oil Prices Surge Amid Ship Attack in Strait of Hormuz and Logistics Risks

Key summary
  • International oil prices (Brent) rose amid spreading concerns over Middle East supply disruptions, including the attack on Saudi Arabia's King Fahd Airport, while Asian stock markets fell amid Gulf tensions and caution ahead of tech earnings.
  • A Kuwaiti-flagged tanker carrying 21 Indian crew members was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, though all crew members were confirmed safe, with concerns over vessel safety in the strait persisting.
  • With the prolonged US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's stockpiled oil from its 'shadow fleet' for exports to Asia has reportedly been completely depleted, signaling a visible weakening of Iran's crude export capacity.
  • According to an exclusive domestic media report, 7 tankers linked to Sinokor Merchant Marine were found to have been placed on Iran's blacklist, exposing them to the risk of seizure and confiscation, highlighting concrete risks for South Korea's shipping industry in transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

This page automatically collects and summarizes public news coverage and material from relevant institutions across Qatar, Iran, other major countries and Korea. News is gathered by querying Google News RSS feeds, Naver News search, and outlet RSS (Al Jazeera, BBC, etc.) with keywords such as Qatar, the Middle East and energy; in-depth reports are collected directly from the publication boards and RSS of domestic and international research institutes, international organizations and consultancies (supplemented by news search targeting those publishers), keeping only analyses and reports on the Middle East situation, the Iran war and their industrial, supply-chain and energy repercussions. The report list accumulates items published since the war's outbreak (2026-02-28), split into domestic and overseas and ordered by publication date (newest first). Collection and summarization rely on each outlet's publicly available headline and snippet; for subscription or paywalled outlets, the full article can be opened through the provided source link only after the reader signs in or subscribes to that outlet directly. The collected articles are automatically clustered and summarized by issue, and translated into English and Arabic, by Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5) AI. The whole process runs and publishes automatically twice a day (07:00 and 15:30 Qatar time) via GitHub Actions. The Qatar government activity section separately curates only official statements, announcements and actions on the war and regional situation by Qatar government and state entities — the Emir, the Prime Minister, the ministries of Foreign Affairs, Defense and Interior, the Government Communications Office (GCO), QatarEnergy and the state news agency (QNA). Owing to automated collection some articles or reports may be missed, so please re-verify important issues against the original sources and further searches.
- Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Qatar, Commercial Section · KOTRA Doha
